note: Held-out corpus for ProseShape 1.4.1, written and frozen on 2026-10-04 before any 1.4.1 change and never used for iteration. The 1.4.0 held-out corpus (evals/heldout/) becomes development data for 1.4.1. k01-k12 are synthetic; every name, organization, study, figure and quotation in them is fictional. k13-k15 are human-written excerpts (sources and licenses below and in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md). None of the texts overlap ProseShape's fixtures, examples, or earlier corpora.
user_request: Please humanize this so it reads like a person wrote it. Keep the facts and meaning the same.

sources.k13_human_austen: Jane Austen, Pride and Prejudice (1813), chapter 13. Public domain. Text from Project Gutenberg #1342 (https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/1342). Line breaks unwrapped; Gutenberg's _underscore_ italics converted to *asterisks* and its -- to an em dash, as printed.
sources.k14_human_go_blog: Rob Pike, 'Errors are values', The Go Blog, 12 January 2015 (https://go.dev/blog/errors-are-values). Text licensed CC BY 4.0, code BSD. Opening paragraphs; HTML converted to Markdown, code blocks fenced, the split inline code `if` `err` `!=` `nil` joined into one span.
sources.k15_human_doctorow: Cory Doctorow, 'Tiktok's enshittification', Pluralistic, 21 January 2023 (https://pluralistic.net/2023/01/21/potemkin-ai/). Licensed CC BY 4.0. First four paragraphs, HTML converted to plain text.

k01_incident_postmortem.category: incident postmortem (Markdown headings, bold-label timeline, numbered action items with owners)
k01_incident_postmortem.expected: cut significance and the closing slogan; keep every time, figure, cause, owner and action item, and the document structure

k02_fundraising_appeal.category: nonprofit fundraising email (subject line, beneficiary story, call to action)
k02_fundraising_appeal.expected: plainer and still persuasive; keep every figure, the deadline, Maria's story, the asks and the link

k03_recipe.category: recipe blog post (intro, ingredient list, numbered steps)
k03_recipe.expected: trim the intro hype; ingredient list, quantities and steps intact

k04_job_posting.category: job posting (three labeled lists, salary, closing slogan)
k04_job_posting.expected: cut hype; keep every responsibility, requirement, figure and benefit and the list structure

k05_science_news.category: science news (hedged findings, two attributed quotations, outside expert)
k05_science_news.expected: keep every hedge, number, caveat and attribution; quotations verbatim; cut the inflated opener and closer
protected: "We were surprised by how consistent the pattern was across different groups,"
"But this is an observational study, so we can't say that napping causes the improvement."

k06_book_review.category: first-person book review with a mixed verdict (italic title, quoted line, rating)
k06_book_review.expected: keep the reviewer's praise and criticisms at their strength, the quoted line verbatim, the italics and the rating
protected: "The tide took what it wanted and returned only what it could not use."

k07_toast.category: wedding toast (personal speech, anecdotes, one staged line)
k07_toast.expected: warm and spoken; keep every person, number and anecdote, the chess and houseplant jokes, and 'finally'; no new anecdotes

k08_childrens_story.category: children's read-aloud fiction (repetition, sound words, stated moral)
k08_childrens_story.expected: keep the read-aloud repetition, the sound words, every event and the stated moral in plainer words
protected: "You don't need to be big to be brave."

k09_fiction_interior.category: literary fiction scene (interior voice, stock sensations, staged contrast in dialogue, realization ending)
k09_fiction_interior.expected: rewrite mode: keep every beat, every line of dialogue in substance, the realization and the ending; tighten stock sensations without inventing actions
protected: four hours every other weekend for two years

k10_help_article.category: help-center article (Markdown headings, numbered steps, bold UI labels, keyboard shortcuts in code)
k10_help_article.expected: cut chatbot residue; steps, UI labels, shortcuts and limits byte-exact

k11_nearclean_garden.category: near-clean human-style neighborhood email with one not-X-but-Y line
k11_nearclean_garden.expected: minimal edit; the contrast line's claim (the garden is where neighbors talk) survives, restated or kept; 'honestly' and 'actually' stay
protected: neighbors actually talk to each other

k12_nearclean_piano.category: near-clean personal essay with meaning-bearing small words and a contrast ending
k12_nearclean_piano.expected: few or no changes; every small word (almost, mostly, quietly, finally, maybe, a little) stays; no added hedges or feelings
protected: mostly holding up mail and a lamp

k13_human_austen.category: already-good human literary fiction (1813): period spelling, italics, dialogue dashes
k13_human_austen.expected: few or no changes; period spelling (to-day, favour), italics and dashes untouched
protected: Why, Jane—you never dropped a word of this—you sly thing!

k14_human_go_blog.category: already-good human technical prose with code blocks and a deliberate triad
k14_human_go_blog.expected: few or no changes; code blocks and inline code byte-exact; the triad and the short emphatic lines are the author's
protected: This is unfortunate, misleading, and easily corrected.
Values can be programmed, and since errors are values, errors can be programmed.

k15_human_doctorow.category: already-good human polemic with a strong personal voice (coinage, profanity, first-then-finally list)
k15_human_doctorow.expected: few or no changes; the voice, the coinage and the profanity stay
